E1.evidence: Issue #5850 gives a reproducer ("easy to reproduce by introducing a sleep, e.g. `std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));`, in `AmclNode::updateParametersCallback` (just after the lock)") and a second contributor confirmed it ("I did a quick test on the Jazzy branch and was able to reproduce the issue"); PR #5852 was merged (main 0b93eeb3, 2026-01-29).

units_identified: parameter client (ros2 param CLI or the reporter's stack)
E2.evidence: The deadlock is between two threads inside the amcl process: the parameter callback (AmclNode::updateParametersCallback, which re-initialises the laser subscribers/message filters on a scan_topic change) and the laser callback that ran in a separate callback group/thread. The reporter: "It seems that AMCL has a deadlock issue when changing a dynamic parameter  that triggers a `reinit_laser`, for instance `ros2 param set /amcl scan_topic XXX`" and "My bet is on a thread issue when having to reset the laser subscribers/messafe filters". The fix removes the callback group from the laser subscription options in AmclNode::initMessageFilters ("[AMCL] Use main thread for laser callback"). The failure does not depend on any assumption between amcl and the peer that sets the parameter; any correct parameter client setting a valid scan_topic triggers it.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated as an interface operation: the failing interaction is internal to one process (a dynamic parameter update racing the laser callback thread).

E4.evidence: Observed deadlock of amcl on a dynamic parameter change; fixed version reported working: "This one now runs on the Dexory fleet without issues."

ineligible_reason: E2 step 2 (internal): a thread deadlock inside the amcl node between its parameter-update callback and its laser callback group; it occurs with any correct peer that sets the parameter.
notes: Environment reported: Kilted, nav2 main from source, Cyclone DDS; also reproduced on the Jazzy branch by mini-1235, who suspected navigation2 PR #2483 as the origin. The TF timer keeps its callback group (maintainer: "Leave the TF timer, that seems on first glance to be important.").
